pveClusters.title: PVE Targets

pveClusters.backupJobRetentionHint: The intended, primary place for retention is a PBS Prune Job on the target datastore (Datastores page) — this job-level setting is offered because PVE itself supports it and some existing jobs already use it. Setting both here and as a PBS Prune Job risks conflicting policies.

pveClusters.retentionComparisonGap: Neither this job nor a PBS Prune Job sets retention here — backups to this datastore will never be pruned automatically.
pveClusters.retentionComparisonAuthCaveat: This compares configured policy only. Whether this job's own retention actually runs also depends on the PBS credential stored inside PVE's own storage configuration for this target — RESURGAM cannot inspect what that credential is permitted to do.
pveClusters.confirmDeleteBackupJobBody: The {{schedule}} vzdump schedule will be permanently removed from this PVE cluster.

datastores.title: Datastores
datastores.maintenanceMessage: Message (shown to anyone hitting this datastore)
datastores.attestationIntro: RESURGAM cannot observe write-immutability on this datastore directly — record a self-assessment instead, for the 3-2-1-1-0 report leg. Every record is kept as permanent history and attributed to whoever recorded it.
datastores.removedFromPbsHint: PBS no longer lists this datastore (noticed {{date}}). Its tenant assignment and history are kept; it is restored automatically if it reappears on PBS.
datastores.importAutoDiscoveryHint: Datastores are discovered and imported automatically on every Collector sync; use this only to import one right away.
datastores.encryptionKeyConfiguredHint: A PBS encryption key is stored for this datastore, so RESURGAM can index, browse and restore files from encrypted backups.
datastores.encryptionKeyIntro: Only needed if backups on this datastore are encrypted on the client side. Without the key, RESURGAM cannot index, browse or restore their files, or test them in the Recovery Lab. For backups made by PVE, the key is the file /etc/pve/priv/storage/<STORAGE-ID>.enc on a PVE node. Password-protected keys are not supported (same as in PVE).
datastores.encryptionKeyInvalidJson: This doesn't look like a PBS key file (expected JSON with a "data" field).
datastores.encryptionKeyPasswordProtected: This key is password-protected. RESURGAM can only use keys without a password, like PVE.
datastores.encryptionKeyReadFailed: The file could not be read.
datastores.encryptionKeyWriteOnly: The key is stored encrypted and can never be displayed or downloaded again. Keep your own copy (e.g. a paperkey) in a safe place.
datastores.encryptionKeyRemoveBody: RESURGAM will no longer be able to read encrypted backups on this datastore (file indexing, file restore, Recovery Lab). The backups themselves and PBS are not changed.

fileIndex.excludePatternsHint: Regex patterns (one per line) matched against each file/directory's path during indexing. A match skips it entirely — for VM disks, its whole subtree is never walked, not just left out of the index.

fileIndex.guestExecClusterHint: The lab-enabled PVE cluster a "guest_exec_ephemeral" job's disposable clone boots on for this tenant's groups.
fileIndex.fullReindexHint: Every Nth guest-exec index forces a full walk instead of incremental, reconciling deleted/renamed files an incremental pass can never see.

methodHint.external_mount: PBS file-restore/catalog tools browse the snapshot externally -- works for every backup type, but can't see inside an encrypted disk and has no true incremental indexing.
methodHint.guest_exec_live: A PVE hookscript indexes the live production VM right after its own real backup completes. Genuinely incremental; runs against the live guest, not a clone. VM only.
methodHint.guest_exec_ephemeral: Experimental. Boots a disposable clone of the snapshot, indexes it, destroys it. Never touches production, but every run is a full boot straight from PBS: it needs fast PBS reads, and on slow PBS storage runs can fail. Meant for disks RESURGAM can't read from outside (e.g. encrypted). For ordinary VMs use External mount. VM only.

fileIndex.confirmDeleteBody: This also permanently deletes every indexed entry for this tenant. Indexing can be re-enabled later, but the index itself will need to be rebuilt from scratch.

pbs.tokenIdDetails: The token ID is the user, the realm and the token name joined with '!'. In the PBS web interface: Configuration > Access Control > API Token. It is listed there as the token's ID, e.g. resurgam@pbs!resurgam.
pbs.tokenSecretDetails: PBS shows the secret only once, in the dialog right after you click 'Add' under Configuration > Access Control > API Token. If you no longer have it, create a new token (or use 'Regenerate'). Paste only the secret here, not the whole token.
pbs.credentialsIntro: RESURGAM logs in to PBS once, creates a dedicated API token for this user and grants it the roles Audit, DatastoreAdmin and RemoteAdmin on /. Only the token is stored.
pbs.permissionsIntro: RESURGAM's PBS token needs these privileges. Granting them on / with propagation covers all datastores and remotes. With an API token, its rights are limited to what its user has, so the user needs them too.

pve.tokenIdDetails: The token ID is the user, the realm and the token name joined with '!'. In the PVE web interface: Datacenter > Permissions > API Tokens. It is listed there as 'Token ID', e.g. resurgam@pve!resurgam.
pve.tokenSecretDetails: PVE shows the secret only once, in the dialog right after you click 'Add' under Datacenter > Permissions > API Tokens. If you no longer have it, create a new token. Paste only the secret here, not the whole token.
pve.credentialsIntro: RESURGAM logs in to PVE once, creates a dedicated, privilege-separated API token for this user, creates (or updates) the role RESURGAM with exactly the required privileges and grants it to the token on /. Only the token is stored.
pve.permissionsIntro: RESURGAM's PVE token needs these privileges. Granting them on / with propagation covers all nodes, VMs, storages, SDN and pools. With privilege separation a token's rights are limited to what its user has, so the user needs them too (unless it is root@pam).

pbs.Sys_Audit: Read version, node status and task history (Collector, connection test).
pbs.Datastore_Audit: List datastores, namespaces, backup groups and snapshots.
pbs.Datastore_Read: Read backup contents for file-level restore and indexing.
pbs.Datastore_Modify: Set maintenance mode and the garbage-collection schedule of a datastore.
pbs.Datastore_Prune: Create, edit and run prune jobs; sync jobs with 'remove vanished'.
pbs.Datastore_Verify: Create, edit and run verify jobs.
pbs.Datastore_Backup: Owner-level access to backup groups (group notes, snapshot ownership) and running sync jobs into a datastore.
pbs.Remote_Modify: Create, edit and delete remotes and sync jobs.
pbs.Remote_Read: Create, edit and run pull sync jobs (read data from the source remote).

pve.Sys_Audit: Read nodes, tasks and vzdump backup jobs (GET /cluster/backup).
pve.Sys_Modify: Create, edit, enable/disable vzdump backup jobs (POST/PUT /cluster/backup).
pve.Datastore_Allocate: Delete volumes of restored/lab VMs on cleanup; apply a backup job's retention (prune-backups) on Run now.
pve.Datastore_AllocateSpace: Allocate disks on the target storage for restores and Recovery Lab clones.
pve.VM_Allocate: Create restored VMs/containers and remove Recovery Lab VMs afterwards.
pve.VM_Audit: List guests and read VM configuration.
pve.VM_Backup: Restore guests from PBS backups and start backup jobs (Backup Jobs → Run now).
pve.VM_Clone: Clone the Recovery Lab probe appliance template.
pve.VM_Config_Network: Rewire NICs (and cloud-init IPs) of restored and Recovery Lab VMs.
pve.VM_Config_Options: Set VM options such as enabling the QEMU guest agent.
pve.VM_PowerMgmt: Start and stop restored and Recovery Lab VMs.
pve.VM_GuestAgent_Audit: Recovery Lab level-1 checks: guest-agent ping and reading guest IP addresses.
pve.SDN_Use: Attach VMs to bridges/VNets (restore targets, isolated Recovery Lab networks).
pve.SDN_Allocate: Create and remove the isolated Recovery Lab SDN zone/VNets.
pve.Pool_Allocate: Create the resource pool that groups Recovery Lab VMs.
pve.Pool_Audit: List resource pools and their members (backup-job target picker, Lab).

connection.secretMissingHint: Imported from a configuration backup: the token ID is known, the token secret still has to be entered under Edit.

labSetup.title: Set up lab compute: {{name}}
labSetup.panelIntro: Guided setup: checks every prerequisite on this cluster, offers pickers and safe fixes, and walks you through installing the lab agent.
labSetup.needsConnection: Available once the connection test succeeds (the cluster must be reachable and accept the token).
labSetup.nextSaves: "Next" saves your choices to the cluster.
labSetup.fixDone: Done: storage "{{storage}}" was changed on PVE and checked again.
labSetup.basicsIntro: Recovery Lab boots backups on this cluster in an isolated network. Choose the node(s) lab runs will use; the following steps check everything those nodes need.
labSetup.labNodesHint: Bridge, storages and template are checked on these nodes. The lab agent must be installed on each of them.
labSetup.networkIntro: Each lab run gets its own isolated VNet in an SDN zone. The probe appliance is the only VM with a second NIC on an existing bridge, to report back to RESURGAM.
labSetup.zoneAuto: Automatic: RESURGAM creates its own Simple zone "resurgam"
labSetup.zoneHint: Only Simple zones work today: lab runs create an untagged VNet, which PVE rejects in VLAN/QinQ/VXLAN/EVPN zones.
labSetup.bridge: Uplink bridge for the probe appliance
labSetup.bridgeHint: An existing bridge (on every lab node) from which the appliance can reach the public backend URL.
labSetup.storageIntro: The lab agent writes the appliance's cloud-init snippet to a snippet storage, and each restored VM's writable overlay to a dir storage on the node.
labSetup.snippetStorageHint: A file-based storage (dir, nfs, cifs, cephfs, btrfs) available on the lab nodes. RESURGAM can add the "snippets" content type.
labSetup.overlayStorageHint: Must match the agent's RESURGAM_LAB_AGENT_OVERLAY_STORAGE_ID. Default path on the node: {{path}}.
labSetup.saveFirst: Save the chosen snippet storage first ("Save and check"), then RESURGAM can add the content type.
labSetup.fixAddSnippetsConfirm: RESURGAM will add the content type "snippets" to storage "{{storage}}" on PVE. All existing content types stay. Undo in PVE: Datacenter > Storage > Edit > Content.
labSetup.fixCreateOverlayConfirm: RESURGAM will create the PVE storage "{{storage}}" (type dir, path {{path}}, content images) restricted to node(s) {{nodes}}. Nothing existing is changed. Undo in PVE: Datacenter > Storage > Remove.
labSetup.fixAddImagesConfirm: RESURGAM will add the content type "images" to storage "{{storage}}" on PVE. All existing content types stay.
labSetup.applianceIntro: Each run clones the probe appliance template. It must be a QEMU VM template with resurgam-lab-prober, qemu-guest-agent, dnsmasq, nftables and nmap installed, on the lab node.
labSetup.templateHint: Only VM templates are listed. If none fits, RESURGAM can build one below.
labSetup.agentIntro: resurgam-lab-agent runs on each lab node: it maps backups as local disks and starts the lab VMs. It only makes outbound HTTPS calls to RESURGAM.
labSetup.rotateWarning: A token already exists. Rotating it immediately locks out every agent still using the old one.
labSetup.tokenShownOnce: The token is shown only now. It is stored hashed and cannot be displayed again.
labSetup.agentBuildHint: This installation ships no prebuilt package: build the .deb from restore-worker/ on a Debian host of the same release as the PVE node (PVE 9 = trixie, PVE 8 = bookworm).
labSetup.agentInstallStep: 3. Install it on each lab node (as root)
labSetup.envNeedsToken: Generate the token first; it is then filled in here.
labSetup.envPbsTokenHint: Fill in RESURGAM_LAB_AGENT_PBS_TOKEN with a PBS API token of this node (at least Datastore.Read on the lab datastores). It never leaves the node.
labSetup.agentWaitStep: 5. Wait for the agent to check in
labSetup.summaryReady: Everything is in place. Enable the cluster as lab compute to use it for Recovery Lab runs.
labSetup.summaryIncomplete: Some prerequisites are still open. Lab runs fail until the items marked "Missing" are fixed.
labSetup.activateWithWarnings: You can enable the cluster as lab compute anyway and finish the open items later; the list of PVE targets shows "Lab incomplete" until then.

privileges.privileges_missing: The PVE token lacks: {{missing}}. Add them to the token's role (pveum role modify RESURGAM --privs "…" --append 1) or reconnect with credentials.
privileges.all_granted: The token holds every privilege the lab needs.

sdn_zone.zone_not_found: Zone "{{zone}}" does not exist. Pick an existing Simple zone or use the automatic zone.
sdn_zone.default_zone_auto_created: No zone chosen: RESURGAM creates its own Simple zone "{{zone}}" on the first run (needs SDN.Allocate).
sdn_zone.zone_type_unsupported: Zone "{{zone}}" is of type {{type}}; lab runs need a Simple zone.
sdn_zone.zone_not_on_nodes: Zone "{{zone}}" is not available on {{missing_nodes}}. Add those nodes to the zone in PVE and apply.
sdn_zone.zone_pending_apply: Zone "{{zone}}" has SDN changes not applied yet. Apply them in PVE (Datacenter > SDN).

uplink_bridge.bridge_ok: Bridge "{{bridge}}" exists on every lab node.

snippet_storage.storage_type_unsupported: Storage "{{storage}}" ({{type}}) cannot hold snippets. Pick a file-based storage.
snippet_storage.snippets_content_missing: Storage "{{storage}}" does not allow "snippets" yet. RESURGAM can add it.
snippet_storage.storage_ok: Storage "{{storage}}" accepts snippets on every lab node.

overlay_storage.storage_not_found: Overlay storage "{{storage}}" does not exist yet. RESURGAM can create it (dir, {{expected_path}}).
overlay_storage.storage_type_not_dir: Storage "{{storage}}" is of type {{type}}; the agent needs a dir storage. Use another overlay storage ID.
overlay_storage.storage_not_on_nodes: Storage "{{storage}}" is not available on {{missing_nodes}}. Add those nodes to it in PVE.
overlay_storage.images_content_missing: Storage "{{storage}}" does not allow "images". RESURGAM can add it.
overlay_storage.storage_marked_shared: Storage "{{storage}}" is marked as shared, but overlays exist only on the node that wrote them.
overlay_storage.storage_ok: Overlay storage "{{storage}}" ({{path}}) is available on every lab node.

appliance_template.not_configured: No probe appliance template chosen yet.
appliance_template.template_not_qemu: Guest {{vmid}} is a container; the appliance must be a VM template.
appliance_template.not_a_template: VM {{vmid}} ({{name}}) is not a template. Convert it to a template in PVE.
appliance_template.template_not_on_lab_node: Template {{vmid}} is on node {{node}}, which is not a lab node; cloning would fail. Migrate it to the lab node.
appliance_template.template_single_node: Template {{vmid}} is on node {{node}} only; lab runs must target that node.
appliance_template.template_version_unknown: Template {{vmid}} carries no RESURGAM build marker, so its resurgam-lab-prober version is unknown (this RESURGAM ships {{shipped_prober_version}}). Rebuild the template with RESURGAM, and again after every update.
appliance_template.template_outdated: Template {{vmid}} has resurgam-lab-prober {{prober_version}}; this RESURGAM ships {{shipped_prober_version}}. Rebuild the template.

lab_agent.never_seen: The agent has never checked in. Install it, fill in the env file and restart it.
lab_agent.stale: The agent last checked in {{minutes}} minute(s) ago. Check: systemctl status resurgam-lab-agent

backend_url.not_configured: RECOVERY_LAB_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL is not set on the backend; agent and appliance can't report back. Set it and restart the API and the lab scheduler.
backend_url.not_https: The public backend URL {{url}} is not HTTPS.

uplink_network.invalid_settings: The uplink settings are inconsistent. Correct the VLAN tag or static range in the network step.
uplink_network.vlan_not_allowed: Bridge "{{bridge}}" is VLAN-aware but does not allow VLAN {{vlan_tag}} on {{nodes}} (bridge-vids). Add the VLAN ID in PVE (System > Network) or use another tag.
uplink_network.bridge_not_vlan_aware: Bridge "{{bridge}}" is not VLAN-aware on {{nodes}}. PVE then uses its "traditional" method (creates <port>.{{vlan_tag}} and {{bridge}}v{{vlan_tag}}), which only works if the bridge's port carries the VLAN. Better: tick "VLAN aware" on the bridge.
uplink_network.overlaps_lab_subnet: The uplink subnet overlaps the lab network of {{overlaps}}; runs of those groups are refused.
uplink_network.range_exhausted: All {{range_size}} uplink addresses are in use by active lab runs; a new run would be refused. Clean up finished runs or widen the range.
uplink_network.dhcp_ok: The uplink gets its address by DHCP.

labSetup.agentDownloadHint: SHA-256: {{sha256}}. Copy the file to the lab node (e.g. with scp) and check it there with sha256sum.

guided.loginStep: 1. Log in to the lab node once over SSH
guided.pbsTokenHint: Written once into /etc/default/resurgam-lab-agent and never stored by RESURGAM. Leave empty to keep a token already set on the node.
guided.installHint: RESURGAM uploads the shipped package to {{node}}, installs it, writes the env file with a freshly generated agent token and starts the service.
guided.waitStep: 3. Wait for the agent to check in

ssh.intro: This login is used for this one operation only: password or key are neither stored nor logged.
ssh.hostFallback: PVE reports no address for this node; the cluster's API address is suggested. Make sure it really is this node.
ssh.hostKeyIntro: {{host}} presents this host key ({{type}}). Nothing has been sent yet.
ssh.hostKeyVerify: Compare it on the node (PVE console) with:
ssh.confirmHostKey: I compared the fingerprint on the node; it matches.
ssh.usernameHint: root, or a user allowed to run sudo without a password.
ssh.oneTime: If the host key no longer matches at login, RESURGAM stops before any credential is sent.

steps.finalize: Clean up and convert to template

errors.host_key_mismatch: The node's host key changed. No credentials were sent. Check the node and confirm the fingerprint again.
errors.auth_failed: The node rejected the login. Check user and password or key.
errors.auth_method_not_allowed: The node does not allow this login method.
errors.privilege_missing: The user is not root and may not run sudo without a password. Log in as root or allow passwordless sudo.
errors.connect_failed: The node cannot be reached over SSH. Check address, port and that RESURGAM may reach the node on that port.
errors.private_key_invalid: The private key could not be read (or the passphrase is wrong).
errors.private_key_passphrase_required: The private key is encrypted: enter its passphrase.
errors.debian_release_mismatch: The node's Debian release does not match the shipped package (built for PVE 9 / Debian 13). See the step log for details.
errors.not_a_pve_node: qm/pvesm are missing on this host: it is not a Proxmox VE node.
errors.install_failed: apt-get could not install the package; its output is shown at the step.
errors.upload_corrupted: The uploaded package was corrupted; nothing was installed. Try again.
errors.service_failed: The service could not be enabled or started.
errors.command_timeout: A command on the node did not finish in time.
errors.tools_missing: Tools are missing on the node (qm, pvesm, pvesh, genisoimage, curl, sha512sum, sha256sum).
errors.vmid_taken: The VMID is already in use. Pick another one or leave the field empty.
errors.node_image_missing: The given base image was not found on the node.
errors.image_download_failed: The node could not download or verify the Debian cloud image. It needs HTTPS access to cloud.debian.org – or upload the image to the node and choose "Image on the node".
errors.snippet_storage_unusable: The snippet storage gives no path for a snippet (is the "snippets" content type missing?).
errors.vm_create_failed: qm create failed; its output is shown at the step.
errors.vm_start_failed: The build VM could not be started.
errors.build_vm_stopped: The build VM stopped before finishing.
errors.build_timeout: The build VM did not answer in time. Usually it has no network on the uplink (bridge/VLAN/IP) or no access to a Debian mirror. The unfinished VM was removed.
errors.build_failed: The installation inside the build VM failed (usually no access to the Debian mirror). The log is shown at the step; the unfinished VM was removed.
errors.prober_version_mismatch: The build VM reports another resurgam-lab-prober version than expected.
errors.finalize_failed: The template could not be finished; the unfinished VM was removed.
errors.internal_error: Unexpected error; details are shown at the step.

uplink.vlanHint: 1–4094; set as tag= on the probe appliance's uplink NIC. Empty = no VLAN tag.
uplink.dhcpHint: The network on the uplink bridge hands out the address.
uplink.staticHint: RESURGAM gives every active lab run its own address from this range (via cloud-init) and frees it when the run is cleaned up.
uplink.fixErrors: Please correct the highlighted uplink fields first.

errors.vlanRange: The VLAN tag must be between 1 and 4094.
errors.prefixRange: The prefix length must be between 8 and 30 (e.g. 24).
errors.dnsRequired: At least one DNS server is needed so the appliance can resolve the backend URL.
errors.notSameSubnet: Start and end are not in the same subnet.
errors.endBeforeStart: The end is before the start.
errors.networkOrBroadcast: That is the subnet's network or broadcast address.
errors.gatewayOutsideSubnet: The gateway is not in the range's subnet.
errors.gatewayInRange: The gateway lies inside the range; shrink the range so the gateway is outside it.

build.title: Build the template with RESURGAM
build.intro: RESURGAM builds the template on the lab node: Debian 13 cloud image, the shipped resurgam-lab-prober package and its tools, a first boot on the lab uplink, then conversion to a template that is selected for this cluster. Rebuild it after every RESURGAM update.
build.vmidHint: Empty = the cluster's next free VMID.
build.imageDownloadHint: The node downloads debian-13-genericcloud-amd64.qcow2 and checks its SHA-512; it needs HTTPS access to cloud.debian.org for that. The build VM also needs a Debian mirror.
build.imageNodeHint: No internet on the node: upload the image first (e.g. via PVE's upload into a storage with content "import") and give its volume ID or an absolute path.
build.scriptHint: Run as root on the node; then pick VMID {{vmid}} as the template above.
build.modeAgent: Build with the paired lab agent on {{node}} (no login)
build.agentHint: Tip: pair the lab node in the 'Lab agent' step and the agent builds the template itself -- no SSH login needed.
build.agentRuns: The lab agent on {{node}} builds the template on its node and reports every step here.

labSetup.agentModePair: Pair node with a one-time code (recommended)

pair.intro: This step shows one command. Paste it into the node's own shell (Proxmox web UI -> node -> Shell): it installs the lab agent, asks for the node's PBS token (it stays on the node) and registers the agent. No SSH login or password is entered here. The code works once and expires after 30 minutes.
pair.openShellHint: Opens the Proxmox web UI's shell for this node in a new tab; you may have to sign in to Proxmox first.
pair.pasteCommand: Paste this command and press Enter
pair.commandHint: The command checks the script's fingerprint before running it. Valid until {{expires}}, once.
pair.paired: Node {{node}} is paired; its agent now reports to RESURGAM.
pair.pbsMissing: No PBS token was entered: template builds work, lab runs need it — add it on the node in /etc/default/resurgam-lab-agent and restart resurgam-lab-agent.
pair.expired: This code can no longer be used. Create a new one.

updates.unavailable: Updates can only be installed on the RESURGAM appliance.

upload.title: Upload update bundle
upload.description: Select a signed resurgam-<version>.bundle file (max. {{limit}}). It is verified automatically after the upload.
upload.tooLarge: The file is larger than the upload limit of {{limit}}.
upload.notABundle: This file is not a RESURGAM update bundle (not a tar archive). Select the resurgam-<version>.bundle file of the release.
upload.failed: The upload failed. Check the connection and try again.

verify.title: Bundle check
verify.waiting: Waiting for the updater on the appliance to check the bundle…
verify.reconnecting: Connection to the backend lost, retrying…

apply.confirmText: RESURGAM is updated from {{from}} to {{to}}. A database backup is taken first; if anything fails, the previous version is restored automatically. The web interface is unavailable for a few minutes while the services restart.

progress.title: Update to {{version}}
progress.queued: Waiting for the updater on the appliance to start…
progress.restarting: Restarting… the services are being replaced. This page reconnects automatically.

result.rolledBack: The update failed and version {{version}} was restored. Reason:
result.failed: The update failed before anything was changed. Reason:

errors.requestFailed: The request could not be sent. Try again.

backups.title: Database backups
backups.description: Taken automatically before every update; the last 5 are kept on the appliance.

updateSource.title: Update source
updateSource.description: Where new RESURGAM releases are published. Paste the repository's web address -- GitHub (default) or GitLab work the same way. RESURGAM looks for releases newer than the installed version that carry a signed resurgam-<version>.bundle; a downloaded bundle is verified against the release key exactly like an uploaded one, and nothing is installed without your confirmation.
updateSource.tokenStored: Stored -- leave empty to keep it
updateSource.tokenNone: Only needed for a private repository
updateSource.tokenHintGithub: Fine-grained token with read-only access to this repository's Contents (or a classic token with repo). Without a token GitHub allows 60 requests per hour.
updateSource.tokenHintGitlab: Personal access token with read_api (an asset in GitLab's package registry may need api).
updateSource.tlsWarning: TLS verification is off: the access token travels without protection against an attacker in the network. The bundle signature is still checked.
updateSource.removed: Update source removed. Bundles already downloaded stay in the bundle list.
updateSource.removeConfirmBody: RESURGAM stops looking for new releases and the stored access token is deleted. Bundles already downloaded stay in the bundle list. You can set up the source again at any time.
updateSource.tokenCleared: The repository is now on another host, so the stored access token was removed instead of being sent there. Enter a token for the new repository if it is private.
updateSource.storedTokenWithheld: The stored access token belongs to the saved repository host and was not sent to this one — the test ran without a token. Enter the token for this repository to test it with one.

errors.requestFailed: The request could not be sent. Try again.

releases.title: Available releases
releases.noBundleHint: Release {{version}} has no resurgam-{{version}}.bundle asset, so it cannot be installed from here.
releases.applianceOnly: Releases can only be downloaded and installed on the RESURGAM appliance.

download.succeeded: Bundle {{version}} downloaded -- it is being verified below.

export.title: Export configuration
export.description: Downloads this instance's configuration as a JSON file: settings (including the MFA requirement), branding and app title, the update source, tenants, PBS and PVE connections, datastore assignments, policies, pricing plans, users and roles, and Recovery Lab application groups. Secrets are never included (API token secrets, passwords, MFA factors, OIDC client secret, SMTP password, encryption keys, the update source's access token) — they must be entered again after an import. Backup history, tasks and reports are not part of it.

import.title: Import configuration
import.description: Choose a file from "Export configuration". RESURGAM first checks it without changing anything and shows what would be created, updated, skipped or is in conflict. Existing objects are matched by tenant slug, host and port, datastore name and email; nothing is deleted.
import.notJson: This file is not valid JSON. Choose a file created by "Export configuration".
import.dryRunOk: Dry run complete, nothing changed yet: {{count}} object(s) would be created or updated.
import.dryRunConflicts: Dry run complete, nothing changed yet: {{count}} conflict(s) will be left untouched -- check the details below.
import.confirmText: {{count}} object(s) are created or updated in one transaction. Conflicts are skipped. Secrets must be entered afterwards.
import.applied: The configuration was imported. Enter the secrets listed below.

reenter.titleDryRun: Would have to be entered again after the import

diskMounts.title: Disk Mounts
diskMounts.description: Mount a VM backup's disks read-only in a temporary helper VM and reach them over SMB or NFS -- for whole folders, forensic checks or tools that need a real file system. Removed automatically when the lifetime ends.
diskMounts.notSetUp: No lab cluster is set up for disk mounts yet. Ask a platform admin to build the share helper template (Disk Mounts -> Setup).
diskMounts.notSetUpAdmin: No lab cluster is set up for disk mounts yet. Open Setup: it needs the lab agent, a snippet storage and the share helper template.
diskMounts.noLabClustersHint: Disk mounts run on a cluster flagged as lab compute. Set one up under Infrastructure -> PVE targets first.
diskMounts.helperTemplateHint: Built by RESURGAM below; an existing template VMID can be entered instead. Empty turns disk mounts off for this cluster.

problem.agent_token_missing: resurgam-lab-agent is not installed (no agent token).
problem.agent_not_seen: resurgam-lab-agent has not checked in during the last minutes.
problem.snippet_storage_missing: No snippet storage is configured (Lab Compute setup).
problem.helper_template_missing: The share helper template is missing.

diskMounts.awaitingOtherApprover: Another operator has to approve it.
diskMounts.stopQuestion: Stop the share now? The helper VM is removed and connected clients lose access.

volReason.unsupported: File system not supported (e.g. ReFS, ZFS)
volReason.lvm_activation_failed: LVM volume group could not be activated

diskMounts.vmOnlyHint: Only VM backups have disks. For container and host backups use Recovery -> Files.
diskMounts.noDisks: This snapshot has no disk images.
diskMounts.disksHint: Every selected disk is attached read-only; all readable partitions on it are shared.
diskMounts.approvalHint: This cluster requires a second operator's approval before the helper is started.
diskMounts.nodeHint: Must be the node resurgam-lab-agent runs on -- the backup's disks are mapped there.
diskMounts.vlanInvalid: The VLAN tag must be between 1 and 4094.
diskMounts.clientsRequiredNfs: Required for NFS (it has no password): one IPv4 address or network per line, at most a /8.
diskMounts.clientsOptional: Optional: restricts SMB to these addresses or networks (one per line).
diskMounts.lifetimeHint: Counts from when the share is ready; extendable. Afterwards the helper is removed automatically.
diskMounts.reviewReadOnly: The disks are attached read-only and mounted read-only; nothing can be written to the backup.
diskMounts.createdQueued: The helper VM is being started; the connection details appear in the list once it is ready (usually a few minutes).
diskMounts.createdPending: The mount waits for a second operator's approval. Keep the password now — it is not shown again.
diskMounts.passwordOnce: The password is shown only now and is not stored by RESURGAM. Lost it? Stop the mount and create a new one.
diskMounts.forceFinishQuestion: End this mount without waiting for the lab agent? RESURGAM stops retrying the removal and frees its address. Anything still on the node (helper VM, mapped disks, snippet) is listed in the mount's error and has to be removed by hand.
diskMounts.buildWithAgentHint: The paired lab agent on {{node}} builds it — no login needed.
diskMounts.orOverSsh: Or build it over a one-time SSH login:

backupJobReenable.label: Re-enable automatically
backupJobReenable.customInvalid: Enter a whole number of hours from 1 to {{max}}.
backupJobReenable.hintNever: The job stays disabled until someone enables it again.
backupJobReenable.hintTimer: RESURGAM enables the job again automatically when the time is up. You can enable it earlier or cancel the timer at any time.
backupJobReenable.changeBody: The job stays disabled. Choose when RESURGAM should enable it again, counted from now. Nothing is changed in PVE until then.

backupRun.confirmBody: Starts the backup right away on cluster {{cluster}} with the job's storage, mode, compression and retention (prune) settings — like a scheduled run or Proxmox's own “Run now”. Older backups are pruned according to the job's retention. You can follow it live.
backupRun.noPrivileges: The PVE token lacks the needed privileges
backupRun.title: Backup “{{job}}” — live status
backupRun.intro: One backup task per node. The log updates every two seconds; closing this window does not stop the backup.
backupRun.skipped: Not backed up — no longer on the cluster: {{vmids}}
backupRun.skippedOtherNode: Not backed up — the job is bound to one node and these guests run on another: {{vmids}}
backupRun.waitingForLog: Waiting for the first log lines…

alertMailer.title: Alert mailer
alertMailer.intro: Emails this tenant's alarms (overdue backups, datastore capacity) to the recipients below. One summary mail per change: new, escalated to critical, resolved, and optional reminders. Needs mail delivery set up in System Settings → Mail.
alertMailer.recipientsHint: One address per line, or separated by commas. Up to 10.
alertMailer.notifyResolved: Mail when an alarm is resolved
alertMailer.reminderHint: Hours (1–720). Empty: each alarm is mailed once, and again only if it escalates.
alertMailer.lastError: Last delivery failed: {{error}} The mailer retries automatically.
alertMailer.testFailed: Test mail could not be sent: {{error}}

instantRecovery.clusterPanelIntro: Runs a VM straight from its PBS backup within minutes; its disks are moved to storage later, while it runs. Needs resurgam-lab-agent on one node of this cluster (paired with a PBS token) and an overlay storage for the writes. Set both up with the setup wizard; Lab compute itself does not have to be switched on.
instantRecovery.setUpAgent: Set up agent and overlay storage
instantRecovery.alarmHours: Alarm after (hours running from the backup)
instantRecovery.allowEditHint: Restore operators may then run VMs of this cluster straight from their backups (ADR 0030). The VM runs on the agent's node.
instantRecovery.method_full: Full restore — copy the backup, then start
instantRecovery.method_instant: Instant Recovery — run the VM from the backup now, move it to storage later
instantRecovery.methodHint: VMs only. The VM starts within minutes and reads its disks from PBS until you move it to storage. Only clusters with Instant Recovery allowed are listed.
instantRecovery.noClusterAllowed: No cluster allows Instant Recovery yet. A platform admin can allow it in the cluster's settings.
instantRecovery.nodeHint: The VM runs on {{node}}, where the cluster's agent runs.
instantRecovery.storageHint: {{storage}} is where the disks are moved to later. EFI and TPM state are written there right at the start.
instantRecovery.startsAlways: An instantly recovered VM always starts as soon as its disks are mapped.
instantRecovery.listIntro: Instant Recoveries that still use a backup or left something behind. Move each to storage or discard it.
instantRecovery.riskNote: This VM reads its disks from PBS through the agent on its node. If PBS restarts, or PBS, the network to it or the node is gone even briefly, its disks stop working for good: the guest gets I/O errors, and RESURGAM marks the recovery as failed within about two minutes. Then only Discard is left. Move it to storage as soon as you can.
instantRecovery.agentSilent: The agent has not reported for over 5 minutes. The VM may still run, but RESURGAM can't see it.
instantRecovery.macNew: new (the original VM runs or its state is unknown)
instantRecovery.original_unknown: unknown (a cluster could not be reached)
instantRecovery.skippedDevices: Left out because they can't come along: {{devices}} (disks not in the backup, passthrough devices).
instantRecovery.discardBody: VM {{vmid}} is stopped and deleted, with everything written since it started from the backup. The backup itself was never written to and stays as it is.
instantRecovery.maintenanceWarning: VMs run straight from backups on this datastore: {{vms}}. Maintenance mode can cut them off their disks (I/O errors in the guest). Move them to storage first, or confirm to continue anyway.
instantRecovery.pbsWarning_one: 1 VM runs straight from a backup on this PBS ({{datastores}}). Stopping PBS, its network or the datastore gives it I/O errors.
instantRecovery.pbsWarning_other: {{count}} VMs run straight from backups on this PBS ({{datastores}}). Stopping PBS, its network or the datastore gives them I/O errors.

encryption.keyChangedHint: The newest backup uses a different encryption key (or none) than the backup before it. Older and newer backups need different keys to restore.
encryption.keysInUseHint: {{count}} encrypted backups in this datastore, by key fingerprint.
